title: The simplicial homotopy category preserves binary products
statement:
Use simplicial sets and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For any simplicial set $S$, define $hS$ as the category of vertices and finite composable edge words, modulo the relations that degenerate edges are identities and the long edge of a $2$-simplex is the composite of its successive edges. A simplicial map induces a functor by applying it to vertices and edge words. For any two small simplicial sets $K,L$ in a common universe, the canonical comparison functor induced by the two projections is an isomorphism of ordinary categories
$$h(K\times L)\longrightarrow hK\times hL.$$
The comparison is natural in both simplicial sets and includes empty inputs.

from.place: Proof paragraph 2, displayed derived R Hom / R lim calculation: coherent diagram realization through finite-Reedy localization, at the source-attachment join/cone comparison. Legitimate ordinary pullback of the cone comparison over a varying joint endpoint base. Identification of Joyal fibrations and weak equivalences between quasicategories, used to factor the graph of the comparison. At this identification, interval boundary tests replace an uncited appeal to the fibration clause; they do not identify equivalence-edge lifting by themselves. Supporting universe comparison in the interval-boundary proof: the same-universe hFun tests imply the enlarged-universe hFun tests. The product comparison supplies the naturality of interval homotopies on ordinary homotopy categories in interval-boundary proof step 8.
